digest.en: The Mecca pact reaches Tehran as Saudi Arabia seeks Chinese missile support under Houthi fire. Meanwhile, the UN warns the ocean’s carbon absorption is weakening while Sudan’s El Obeid civilians face drone strikes.
digest.hi: ईरान और इज़राइल के बीच जारी संघर्ष ने इस घंटे में 47 अरब डॉलर का सैन्य खर्च दर्ज किया, हर छह हफ्ते में 3.5 अरब डॉलर बढ़ रहा है।

articles.title: GLP-1 weight-loss pills vs injections: How do they compare and why you shouldn't get the pills
articles.summary: Singapore offers Wegovy only as a weekly injection. The daily pill version remains unavailable locally. Doctors caution that the medication targets obesity, not casual weight loss. Side effects and dosing differences distinguish the two delivery methods. Wegovy, a GLP-1 weight-loss drug, is already available in Singapore as a once-weekly weight-loss injection. Now offered as a daily pill in several countries but not Singapore, how does it compare with the jab?

articles.title: US ambassador suggests Trump could blame Canada if midterms don’t go his way
articles.summary: US ambassador Pete Hoekstra suggested Canada might face blame if Republicans lose next week's midterms. He previously accused Canadian officials of interfering in American elections. His comments have intensified a bitter dispute between the two nations. Pete Hoekstra, controversial US ambassador to Canada, has also accused Canadian officials of interfering in US electionsThe US ambassador has suggested Canada could be blamed if Republicans perform poorly in next week’s midterm elections, the latest intervention from a controversial figure who has been accused of inflaming a bitter dispute that has angered and baffled residents of both countries. O.

articles.title: The Mecca pact goes to Tehran. Can it keep the region out of another war?
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey sent senior officials to Tehran to negotiate with Iran under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement. Prince Khalid bin Salman, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Ibrahim Kalın met President Pezeshkian and security chief Mohsen Rezaei. The unusual diplomatic move aims to prevent regional escalation through direct dialogue. On Monday, the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement did something a defense treaty is not usually built to do.

articles.title: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid trapped between drones and incarceration
articles.summary: UN investigators reported that El Obeid civilians face drone strikes from the Rapid Support Forces. They also endure arbitrary arrests by the Sudanese Armed Forces. Residents live in constant fear of both military threats and state detention. Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid live in constant fear of drone attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and of a wave of arbitrary arrests by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), UN-appointed independent investigators said on Wednesday.

articles.title: UN human rights chief urges better protection of civilians in conflicts
articles.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk highlighted youth-led protests in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Madagascar. He said these movements show a growing global demand for stronger human rights protections. The protests focus on corruption and inequality. Youth-led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing demand for reinforcing human rights around the world, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

articles.title: Ending conflict is ‘number one thing’ to reduce world hunger, new WFP chief says
articles.summary: Luke Lindberg, the new head of the UN World Food Programme, stated that ending conflict is the primary solution to global hunger. He noted that war drives two thirds of acute food insecurity affecting 266 million people worldwide. Lindberg emphasized that peace is the most effective tool for reducing starvation. Reducing conflict is the single most effective way to tackle global hunger, the new head of the UN World Food Programme (WFP), Luke Lindberg, said on Wednesday, noting that conflict drives two thirds of the acute food insecurity affecting 266 million people worldwide.

articles.title: Ocean’s ability to absorb carbon is weakening as climate change intensifies, UN warns
articles.summary: A new UN report states the ocean's carbon absorption capacity has dropped by six percent. The sea still takes in 30 percent of human emissions. It also absorbs 90 percent of excess heat. This warning arrives ahead of the November COP31 climate conference. The ocean absorbs around 30 per cent of human-caused carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and 90 per cent of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases.

articles.title: Under Houthi fire, Saudi Arabia looks to China for missile support
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is expanding a ballistic missile factory near al-Duwadimi to produce longer-range weapons. The facility sits 200 kilometers west of Riyadh. The move aims to bolster strategic deterrence against Houthi attacks. Media reports confirm the shift toward heavier payload capabilities. Saudi Arabia’s rapid expansion of a ballistic missile factory signals a transformative shift in its pursuit of strategic deterrence.

articles.title: South Korea’s rich lobbying spree isn’t paying off in DC
articles.summary: A House Judiciary Committee report accuses South Korea of targeting American firms with coercive investigations and excessive fines. The findings suggest Seoul's lobbying efforts in Washington have failed to resolve these trade disputes. The report highlights ongoing friction between the two economies. Republicans on the House Judiciary Committee released in July an interim staff report accusing South Korea of “discriminatory attacks on American-owned businesses.” Seoul’s “practices include coercive investigation tactics, overly burdensome regulatory requirements, and massive fines and penalties intended to punish American businesses and make it harder for them to effectively compete against Kor.

articles.title: Scorched earth isn’t driving Ukrainians to sue for peace
articles.summary: Vladimir Putin believes relentless bombing of Ukrainian cities will force Kyiv to sue for peace. This marks his latest shifting theory of victory after earlier land offensives stalled. Polling data suggests this scorched earth strategy is not actually driving Ukrainians toward accepting a negotiated settlement. Vladimir Putin has a theory of victory in Ukraine. It’s not the Russian president’s first theory – that was a quick, dayslong campaign – nor his second or third, which involved different land offensives in the east that quickly petered out.

articles.title: Why Russia's Central Crimean Drone Base Is Hard For Ukraine To Destroy
articles.summary: Satellite imagery reveals a military airfield in central Crimea now functions as a primary hub for Russian drone launches. A Crimean military insider told RFE/RL that the site’s dispersed layout makes it difficult for Ukrainian forces to target effectively. The base uses multiple, smaller launch pads rather than a single concentrated runway. This fragmentation reduces the impact of any single precision strike. Ukraine has struggled to neutralize the facility despite repeated attempts. The infrastructure remains operational and continues to support Russian drone operations against Ukrainian targets.

articles.title: 'Committed To European Integration': Student List's Srdanovic On Serbia's Post-Vucic Future
articles.summary: Ilija Srdanovic, the lead candidate for Serbia’s Student List, confirmed the party’s commitment to European integration following Aleksandar Vucic’s defeat. The student-led opposition movement secured victory, ending over a decade of Vucic’s political dominance. Srdanovic outlined the next steps for the country in an interview with RFE/RL’s Balkan Service. The transition marks a significant shift in Serbian political leadership. Aleksandar Vucic’s election defeat has ended more than a decade of political dominance and handed victory to Serbia’s student-led opposition movement.

articles.title: Serbia Student List Lead Candidate Vows EU Integration, Open Debate On Russia Ties
articles.summary: Ilija Srdanovic leads Serbia's Student List party. The group recently ousted Aleksandar Vucic in elections. Srdanovic pledged to pursue EU integration. He also proposed a public debate on reconsidering sanctions against Russia. In an interview with RFE/RL, Ilija Srdanovic, the lead candidate for Serbia's Student List -- which ousted longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in recent elections -- pledged to pursue EU integration and said Belgrade's stance on sanctions against Russia could be reconsidered through public debate.

articles.title: 'Get Killed Or Starve': Life Under Russian Occupation In Oleshky
articles.summary: Residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky face severe food shortages and threats. Civilians risk mines and drone attacks to escape the area. A proposed cease-fire could open a humanitarian corridor. This would allow trapped civilians to leave the Ukrainian city. Residents fleeing Russian-occupied Oleshky describe hunger, soaring food prices, and threats from Russian soldiers. Cut off from supplies, civilians risk mines and drone attacks to escape.

articles.title: General Assembly weighs US embargo against Cuba ahead of 34th vote
articles.summary: The United Nations General Assembly began its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba. Member states will vote on Wednesday, 28 October, to end the sanctions. This will be the 34th consecutive annual resolution calling for the immediate termination of the trade restrictions. The General Assembly opened its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba on Tuesday.

articles.title: Record carbon dioxide levels will impact us for centuries, says UN weather agency
articles.summary: The World Meteorological Organization reported that carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases hit record highs in 2025. Burning fossil fuels drove these levels, locking in additional long-term global warming. The agency warned these atmospheric changes will affect the planet for centuries. Levels of carbon dioxide (CO2) and other major greenhouse gases in the atmosphere caused by burning fossil fuels reached record highs in 2025, locking in more long-term global warming, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Chinese markets lose trillions as race for AI supremacy with US takes its toll
articles.summary: Chinese stock markets lost trillions of dollars recently. Investors worry about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boom. The race for supremacy against the United States is straining profits and raising concerns about the sector’s future. Lack of profits and the threat posed by western countries are raising concern about the sustainability of Beijing’s AI boomTrillions of dollars have been wiped from China’s stock markets in recent months amid increasing anxiety about the future of artificial intelligence, as Beijing races against the United States for dominance in the sector. The STAR 50 Index, which tracks technology and innovatio.

articles.title: Cease-Fire in Ukraine's Oleshky Expanded To Help Flow Of Aid, Safe Passage
articles.summary: Russian air strikes hit Kyiv on October 26, targeting a university dormitory and other civilian buildings. At least one person died in the attacks. President Zelenskyy urged international partners to supply Ukraine with adequate defensive capabilities. Russian air attacks struck Kyiv late on October 26, hitting a university dormitory and other civilian sites, leaving at least one dead, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on Ukraine's partners to provide the "proper tools" for the country to defend itself.

articles.title: What Now For Serbia After Vucic's Stunning Election Defeat?
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic lost the Serbian parliamentary elections to student-led opposition. The ruling party was ousted from power. The new government must now navigate complex relations with the European Union, Russia, and China. Who will lead the next government of Serbia, after Aleksandar Vucic lost parliamentary elections, can the protest movement turn electoral success into stable rule, and what the result could mean for Serbia’s balancing relations with the European Union, Russia, and China?

articles.title: Iran, Regional Countries Agree To Continue Talks After Tehran Meeting
articles.summary: Mecca Defense Alliance partners met in Tehran to address regional conflicts. The snap meeting focused on stabilizing the Middle East. These tensions are currently disrupting global oil and cargo flows across the region. Officials from the so-called Mecca Defense Alliance have gathered for a snap meeting in Tehran as they look to settle conflicts in the Middle East that have left the region reeling and are impacting global flows of oil and other cargo.

articles.title: US forces accused of ‘weaponising’ Somalia’s floods by trapping women and children in the path of
articles.summary: US airstrikes in southern Somalia are pushing civilians toward the rising River Juba. Women and children face drowning risks as they flee al-Shabaab territory. Humanitarian groups accuse the military of weaponizing the flood crisis. The strategy traps vulnerable populations in dangerous waterways. Exclusive: Coordinated airstrikes on territory held by al-Shabaab are driving the civilian population to find refuge alongside a river where rising water levels are a threat to safety.

articles.title: Bizarre hobby takes seed among China’s stressed young adults
articles.summary: Young Chinese adults are increasingly adopting brick collecting as a low-cost hobby. Facing a stagnant job market, many are choosing this over raising children or pets. The trend offers a cheap, low-maintenance alternative to traditional responsibilities in a difficult economic environment. Faced with a stagnant jobs market, many are spurning children or pets in favour of ‘raising bricks’Young adults in China looking for a cheaper, low-maintenance alternative to having children or pets have found an answer: raising bricks. Bricks may not be as cuddly as cats or as life-affirming as human offspring, but they also cost next to nothing.

articles.title: Student-Led Opposition Celebrates In Serbia After Vucic Concedes Election Defeat
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia's October 25 parliamentary elections. The student-led Students' List took a decisive lead in preliminary results. This ends his fourteen-year dominance of Serbian politics. Former President Aleksandar Vucic, who dominated Serbian politics for the past 14 years, conceded defeat in the country's parliamentary elections after polls closed on October 25. Preliminary results showed the movement called Students' List taking a decisive lead.

articles.title: Will Trump Help Putin Win in Ukraine?
articles.summary: Crisis Group experts discussed the widening rift between Washington and Kyiv regarding Ukraine. They analyzed Russia’s intensifying attacks and Europe’s efforts to support Ukraine while facing internal pressure. The conversation explored whether Trump’s administration might inadvertently aid Putin’s objectives in the ongoing conflict. This week on Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group experts Lucian Kim, Stephen Pomper and Fabienne Hara about the latest rift between Washington and Kyiv, Russia’s intensifying attacks and European capitals’ efforts to strengthen Ukraine while themselves under pressure.

articles.title: How Algeria’s Rupture with the UAE Could Roil the Region
articles.summary: Algeria severed diplomatic ties with the United Arab Emirates after years of disagreement over North Africa and the Sahel. Algiers and Abu Dhabi view the dispute differently, but the rivalry now threatens regional stability. The rupture marks a significant escalation in tensions between the two North African and Gulf powers. Algiers has severed diplomatic ties with Abu Dhabi, following years of discord over crises in North Africa and the Sahel.

articles.summary: अमेरिकी रक्षा खुफिया एजेंसी डीआईए ने चीन के गुप्त रीयूजेबल स्पेसप्लेन की पहली स्पष्ट सैटेलाइट तस्वीर जारी की। यह वाहन अमेरिकी एक्स-37बी जैसा दिखता है। चीन के पास 510 से अधिक जासूसी उपग्रह हैं, जिससे अमेरिका की चिंता बढ़ी है। अमेरिकी रक्षा खुफिया एजेंसी डीआईए ने चीन के गुप्त रीयूजेबल स्पेसप्लेन की पहली साफ सैटेलाइट तस्वीर जारी की है. मैक्सार टेक्नोलॉजीज द्वारा ली गई यह तस्वीर दिखाती है कि यह स्पेसक्राफ्ट अमेरिकी स्पेस फोर्स के एक्स-37बी जैसा दिखता है.

articles.summary: अमेरिका ने उत्तर कोरिया के एक नेटवर्क पर प्रतिबंध लगा दिए। आरोप है कि यह नेटवर्क नौकरी के नाम पर धोखाधड़ी करके कमाई से हथियारों के कार्यक्रम को फंड करता था। US sanctions On North Korea: अमेरिका द्वारा उत्तर कोरिया के एक नेटवर्क पर कार्रवाई की गई है। अमेरिकी सरकार ने इस नेटवर्क पर प्रतिबंध लगा दिए हैं। दरअसल, अमेरिका में नौकरी हासिल करने के नाम पर धोखाधड़ी कर कमाई करने और उस पैसे से हथियारों का कार्यक्रम चलाने के आरोप में यह कार्रवाई हुई।

articles.title: कोर्ट को बेड़ियां लगाना चाहते थे मुनीर-शहबाज, अचानक जज ने मार दिया ऐसा 'हथौड़ा', हिल गया पूरा
articles.summary: लाहौर हाईकोर्ट के जज मोहसिन अख्तर कयानी ने पद से इस्तीफा दे दिया। उन्होंने संविधान संशोधन के जरिए न्यायपालिका पर बढ़ते सरकारी नियंत्रण का विरोध किया। प्रधानमंत्री शहबाज शरीफ और सेना प्रमुख आसिम मुनीर पर अदालतों को नियंत्रित करने के आरोप लगे। यह इस्तीफा पाकिस्तान की न्याय व्यवस्था पर गंभीर प्रभाव डालता है। लाहौर हाईकोर्ट के सीनियर जज न्यायमूर्ति मोहसिन अख्तर कयानी ने अपने पद से इस्तीफा दे दिया है.

articles.title: इंडिया गठबंधन की 1 नवंबर की रैली को CJP सपोर्ट करेगी या नहीं? अभिजीत दीपके ने कर दिया ऐलान
articles.summary: अभिजीत दीपके ने इंडिया गठबंधन की 1 नवंबर की रैली का समर्थन किया। कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी ने दिल्ली में होने वाली इस रैली में भाग लेने का ऐलान किया। इंडिया गठबंधन की एक नवंबर को दिल्ली के रामलीला मैदान में होने वाली रैली को कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के फाउंडर अभिजीत दीपके ने सपोर्ट करने का ऐलान किया है. उन्होंने एक्स पर पोस्ट कर लिखा, 'कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी, इंडिया ब्लॉक की 1 नवंबर की रैली को अपना समर्थन देती है.' GYANU MUST GO!
